root_cause: The date picker's blur handler (_onInputBlur) uses a 100ms setTimeout to hide the picker. During this delay, the picker remains visible in the DOM and can trap focus, causing the Tab key to initially move focus to the next field but then immediately return focus to the date field.
repair_strategy: Remove the setTimeout in _onInputBlur so the picker hides immediately when focus leaves the field (unless a picker button interaction is in progress, tracked by _c flag). Also fix _onInputFocus to properly clear any pending timeout using clearTimeout instead of the non-existent sto.clear method.
expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation from the date input to the next form field (guests) works correctly without focus returning to the date field, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Immediate hide on blur could theoretically interfere with picker button clicks if blur fires before click, but the _c flag (set on mousedown) prevents hide during picker interaction.
The blurFieldOnSelect option still calls field.blur() after hide, which is harmless since focus has already moved.
verification_requirements: The journey test passes: Tab from #checkin moves focus to #guests and keeps it there (focus assertion passes).
Form data for checkin (2026-12-04) and guests (2) are both correctly set.
Regression guard: pointer paging months keeps keyboard focus in the date field.
